payload.title: Add secure login to this application.

questions.text: Which login mechanism should be built? Options: (a) email + password, passwords hashed with Node's built-in crypto scrypt, verified in constant time; (b) passwordless magic link emailed via the existing MemoryEmailSender, one-time token exchanged for a session; (c) OAuth/OIDC against an external identity provider (needs a provider, client id/secret and a callback URL). Recommended default: (a) email + password. Note the repo already has an email stub, so (b) is also a natural fit if you prefer no passwords.

How should the logged-in state be carried between requests? Options: (a) an opaque session id stored in an HttpOnly, SameSite=Strict cookie, backed by the existing in-memory SessionStore; (b) a bearer token (opaque or JWT) returned in the JSON body and sent in an Authorization header. Recommended default: (a) HttpOnly cookie backed by SessionStore.

What user-facing surface is required? Options: (a) JSON API only: POST /login, POST /logout, and GET /me returning the current user; (b) JSON API plus a minimal server-rendered HTML login page with a form. Recommended default: (a) JSON API only.

How do the two seeded users (ada@example.com, grace@example.com) get credentials, and is self-service sign-up in scope? Options: (a) seed demo credentials in code for the two users, no sign-up endpoint; (b) add a POST /register endpoint (sign-up) in addition to seeded credentials; (c) seed credentials from environment variables at startup. Recommended default: (a) seeded demo credentials only, sign-up and password reset explicitly out of scope.

Should brute-force protection be part of this mission? Options: (a) yes, an in-memory per-email failed-attempt counter with a temporary lockout after N failures; (b) no, plain login only, rate limiting is out of scope. Recommended default: (a) include a simple in-memory lockout.

Data store and dependencies: should everything stay in-memory (users, credentials, sessions) with no new runtime npm dependencies, using only Node's crypto and Hono's built-in cookie helpers? Options: (a) yes, in-memory and no new dependencies; (b) allow new runtime dependencies (e.g. argon2, bcrypt) but still in-memory; (c) add a persistent store (e.g. SQLite). Recommended default: (a).

answers.answer: (b) passwordless magic link emailed via the existing MemoryEmailSender; the one-time token expires after 15 minutes and is exchanged for a session. No passwords anywhere.
(a) opaque session id in an HttpOnly, SameSite=Lax cookie backed by the existing SessionStore, 24h TTL; logout revokes the session.

(b) JSON API (POST /auth/request with {email}, POST /auth/verify with {token}, POST /auth/logout, GET /me) plus one minimal static HTML page public/login.html that posts the email to /auth/request and shows the response message. No SPA.
Only the two seeded users can log in. Requesting a link for an unknown email must answer exactly like a known one (202, no email sent) to avoid account enumeration. No sign-up endpoint.
(a) yes: in-memory rate limiting on /auth/request per email. CSRF protection, password reset, email verification, MFA and OAuth are explicitly out of scope.
(a) in-memory only, no new runtime dependencies; Node crypto and Hono's cookie helpers are fine.

contract.goal: Implement the passwordless magic-link domain logic as two pure, in-memory TypeScript modules: src/auth/magic-link.ts (issue single-use, 15-minute login tokens for known users and deliver them via the EmailSender; exchange a valid token for a userId) and src/auth/rate-limit.ts (fixed-window per-key request limiter). Both use injected clocks so tests are hermetic. Cover them with tests/auth-magic-link.test.ts and tests/auth-rate-limit.test.ts.
constraints: Repo facts: Node 22, TypeScript strict with NodeNext module resolution (relative imports must end in .js), Hono 4, zod 4, vitest 5. Existing tests: `npx vitest run` passes 20 tests; typecheck is `npx tsc --noEmit`. Follow the style of src/session/store.ts (injected clock, cloned return values).
No new npm dependencies of any kind. Use only node:crypto (randomBytes, createHash) and the existing modules.

Export EXACTLY this public API from src/auth/magic-link.ts so the routes task can consume it without changes: `export interface MagicLinkOptions { users: UserRepo; email: EmailSender; now?: () => number; ttlMs?: number; baseUrl?: string }`, `export const DEFAULT_MAGIC_LINK_TTL_MS = 15 * 60 * 1000`, `export class MagicLinkService { constructor(options: MagicLinkOptions); request(email: string): Promise<void>; verify(token: string): string | undefined }`. request() resolves to void for BOTH known and unknown emails and takes the same code path shape (look up user via users.findByEmail; if unknown, return without sending). verify() returns the userId for a valid, unexpired, unused token and undefined otherwise; a token is consumed on first successful verify (single use) and can never be reused.

Token generation: at least 32 bytes from crypto.randomBytes, encoded base64url. Never store the raw token: store only its SHA-256 hex digest mapped to { userId, expiresAt }. verify() hashes the incoming token and looks up the digest; expired entries (now > expiresAt) are deleted on lookup. Treat an empty or non-string token as invalid without throwing.

Email delivery: send exactly one message through the EmailSender per known-user request, with to = the user's normalized email, subject containing 'Sign in', and text containing both the raw token and a link of the form `${baseUrl}/login?token=<token>` where baseUrl defaults to 'http://localhost:3000'. Tests must assert this using MemoryEmailSender.sent.
Default TTL is DEFAULT_MAGIC_LINK_TTL_MS (15 minutes); ttlMs must be a finite positive number or the constructor throws 'ttlMs must be a finite positive number'. now defaults to Date.now.

Export EXACTLY this public API from src/auth/rate-limit.ts: `export interface RateLimiterOptions { max: number; windowMs: number; now?: () => number }`, `export class RateLimiter { constructor(options: RateLimiterOptions); allow(key: string): boolean; reset(key: string): void }`. allow() records the attempt and returns true while the number of attempts for that key within the current fixed window is <= max; once max attempts have been made within windowMs it returns false until the window has elapsed. Constructor throws 'max must be a positive integer' / 'windowMs must be a finite positive number' for invalid options.

Required test coverage (hermetic, injected clocks): known email sends one email containing the token; unknown email sends nothing and resolves; verify returns the userId for a fresh token; verify returns undefined for a garbage token, for an expired token (now = issuedAt + ttl + 1), and for a token that was already verified once; two requests for the same user produce two distinct tokens that both work independently; rate limiter allows max attempts then denies, and allows again after windowMs; reset() clears a key.
Do not modify any file outside scope.allowed_paths. Do not touch src/app.ts, src/server.ts, package.json or existing tests.
non_goals: Do not add HTTP routes, cookies, or session handling; that is task t-auth-routes.
Do not create public/login.html or update README.md; that is task t-login-page.
No passwords, password hashing, OAuth, MFA, CSRF tokens or persistent storage.

interpretation: Create src/auth/magic-link.ts exporting MagicLinkOptions, DEFAULT_MAGIC_LINK_TTL_MS and MagicLinkService with the exact signatures given. request(email) looks the user up via UserRepo.findByEmail, silently resolves for unknown emails, and for known users generates a 32-byte base64url token, stores only its sha256 hex digest -> {userId, expiresAt}, and sends one email (to normalized user email, subject containing 'Sign in', text containing raw token and `${baseUrl}/login?token=<token>`).

verify(token) hashes the incoming string, looks up the digest, deletes and returns undefined if expired (now > expiresAt), otherwise deletes the entry (single use) and returns userId. Empty/non-string tokens return undefined without throwing.

Create src/auth/rate-limit.ts exporting RateLimiterOptions and RateLimiter with a fixed-window counter per key: the window starts at the first attempt; allow() increments and returns true while count <= max, false afterwards until now >= windowStart + windowMs, at which point a fresh window begins. reset(key) drops the key's state. Constructor validates max (positive integer) and windowMs (finite positive).
Both classes take an injected now: () => number defaulting to Date.now, following src/session/store.ts style. No new dependencies; only node:crypto.
Write tests/auth-magic-link.test.ts and tests/auth-rate-limit.test.ts covering every required scenario using MemoryEmailSender.sent and controllable clocks.
assumptions: Denied attempts in the rate limiter do not extend or restart the window (pure fixed window).
A token at exactly expiresAt (now === expiresAt) is still valid, mirroring SessionStore's boundary semantics and the contract's 'now > expiresAt' rule.
Email text is plain text containing the token on its own line and the link on another; exact wording beyond the contract's requirements is free.
Non-string tokens are guarded at runtime with a typeof check even though the TypeScript signature is string.
risks: The routes task depends on the exact export shapes; any deviation would break it, so I will match the contract signatures verbatim.
Fixed-window limiters allow up to 2*max attempts across a window boundary; this is inherent to the specified algorithm, not a bug.

contract.goal: Wire passwordless login into the Hono app in src/app.ts: POST /auth/request (rate-limited, enumeration-safe, always 202), POST /auth/verify (exchanges a magic-link token for a 24h session carried in an HttpOnly SameSite=Lax cookie), POST /auth/logout (revokes the session and clears the cookie), GET /me (returns the current user or 401), and GET /login (serves public/login.html from disk). Cover the behaviour with tests/auth-routes.test.ts and keep tests/app.test.ts green.
constraints: Repo facts: Node 22, TypeScript strict with NodeNext (relative imports end in .js), Hono 4.13 (import cookie helpers from 'hono/cookie': getCookie, setCookie, deleteCookie), zod 4.5 available, vitest 5. Tests exercise the app via createApp().request(...) with no live server; keep that pattern. Baseline: `npx vitest run` passes 20 tests, `npx tsc --noEmit` is clean.

This task depends on t-magic-link-core, which provides src/auth/magic-link.ts exporting `MagicLinkService` (constructor({ users, email, now?, ttlMs?, baseUrl? }); request(email): Promise<void>; verify(token): string | undefined returning the userId) and `DEFAULT_MAGIC_LINK_TTL_MS`, and src/auth/rate-limit.ts exporting `RateLimiter` (constructor({ max, windowMs, now? }); allow(key): boolean; reset(key): void). Consume these as-is; do NOT edit those files. If they are missing when you start, report a blocker instead of re-implementing them.

Keep createApp backward compatible: the existing call sites createApp() and createApp(users) must keep working. Extend the signature to `createApp(users: UserRepo = new UserRepo(), deps: AppDependencies = {})` where `export interface AppDependencies { sessions?: SessionStore; email?: EmailSender; magicLinks?: MagicLinkService; rateLimiter?: RateLimiter; now?: () => number; baseUrl?: string }`, with defaults: now = Date.now, sessions = new SessionStore(now), email = new MemoryEmailSender(), magicLinks = new MagicLinkService({ users, email, now, baseUrl }), rateLimiter = new RateLimiter({ max: 5, windowMs: 15 * 60 * 1000, now }). Also export `export const SESSION_COOKIE = 'session'` and `export const SESSION_TTL_MS = 24 * 60 * 60 * 1000`.

POST /auth/request: parse JSON body with zod as { email: string (trimmed, must be a valid email) }; invalid JSON or invalid body -> 400 { error: 'invalid request' }. Rate-limit key is the normalized (trim + lowercase) email, applied BEFORE any user lookup so known and unknown emails behave identically; when rateLimiter.allow(key) is false respond 429 { error: 'too many requests' }. Otherwise await magicLinks.request(email) and respond 202 { message: 'If that email is registered, a sign-in link has been sent.' } for both known and unknown emails with byte-identical bodies.

POST /auth/verify: parse JSON body as { token: non-empty string }; invalid -> 400 { error: 'invalid request' }. Call magicLinks.verify(token); undefined -> 401 { error: 'invalid or expired token' }. On success create a session with sessions.create(userId, SESSION_TTL_MS), set the cookie SESSION_COOKIE = session.id with httpOnly: true, sameSite: 'Lax', path: '/', maxAge: SESSION_TTL_MS / 1000 seconds, and secure: true only when the request URL protocol is 'https:' (so local http development works). Respond 200 with the user object serialized like GET /users/:id (createdAt as ISO string).

GET /me: read SESSION_COOKIE; if absent or sessions.get(id) is undefined (expired/revoked) respond exactly 401 { error: 'not authenticated' } (tests/app.test.ts pins this body). Otherwise respond 200 with the user (look up users.findById(session.userId); if the user vanished respond 401 too). Remove the '// TODO: no authentication exists yet' comment.
POST /auth/logout: if the cookie is present call sessions.revoke(id); always delete the cookie (deleteCookie with path '/') and respond 204 with an empty body, even when no session exists.

GET /login: read public/login.html from disk with node:fs/promises using a path resolved relative to the module (new URL('../public/login.html', import.meta.url)); respond 200 text/html with its contents, or 404 { error: 'login page not found' } if the file does not exist. Do NOT create public/login.html in this task; the file is owned by t-login-page. Your tests must not depend on it existing.

Security: never include the token, the userId or whether the email exists in any /auth/request response or log line. Do not expose the session id anywhere except the Set-Cookie header. Do not add CSRF tokens (out of scope per the human).

Required tests in tests/auth-routes.test.ts, all hermetic with an injected `now` and a MemoryEmailSender: (1) request for a seeded email returns 202 and exactly one email is recorded; (2) request for an unknown email returns 202 with the identical body and no email is recorded; (3) 6th request for the same email within the window returns 429; (4) malformed body returns 400; (5) full flow: request -> extract the token from sender.sent[0].text -> verify returns 200 with the user and a Set-Cookie header containing 'session=', 'HttpOnly', 'SameSite=Lax' and 'Path=/' -> GET /me with that cookie returns 200 with the same user; (6) verify with a bogus token returns 401; (7) a token cannot be verified twice; (8) after logout, GET /me with the old cookie returns 401 and logout responds 204; (9) advancing now by more than SESSION_TTL_MS makes GET /me return 401; (10) GET /login returns 404 when the page file is absent OR 200 text/html when present (assert whichever matches the checked-in state without creating the file).
Only edit files in scope.allowed_paths. Do not change package.json, src/server.ts, src/models/user.ts, src/session/store.ts, src/email/stub.ts, or the auth modules.
non_goals: Do not implement token generation, hashing or rate-limit internals; consume t-magic-link-core.
Do not create public/login.html or edit README.md; that is t-login-page.
No sign-up, password, password reset, email verification, MFA, OAuth, CSRF or persistent storage.

contract.goal: Create the minimal static sign-in page public/login.html (a plain HTML form that posts the email as JSON to POST /auth/request and shows the response message; when the page is opened with ?token=... it posts the token to POST /auth/verify and shows the outcome), update README.md to document the passwordless login flow and endpoints, and add tests/login-page.test.ts that verifies the page is served by GET /login and contains the required behaviour.
constraints: Repo facts: Node 22, TypeScript strict NodeNext (relative imports end in .js), Hono 4, vitest 5; tests call createApp().request(...) directly. This task depends on t-auth-routes, which makes GET /login serve public/login.html from disk and provides POST /auth/request ({email} -> 202 with { message }), POST /auth/verify ({token} -> 200 user + session cookie, 401 on bad token), POST /auth/logout (204) and GET /me. Do not edit src/app.ts.

public/login.html must be a single self-contained file: no external scripts, stylesheets, fonts or CDN references, no framework, no build step, and no inline event handler attributes (use addEventListener in one <script> block). Keep it under 150 lines.

Page behaviour: a <form id="request-form"> with <input type="email" name="email" required> and a submit button. On submit, preventDefault, fetch('/auth/request', { method: 'POST', headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' }, body: JSON.stringify({ email }) }) and render the JSON `message` (or `error`) field into an element with id="status" using textContent (never innerHTML). If location.search contains a token parameter, on load call fetch('/auth/verify', { method: 'POST', headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' }, body: JSON.stringify({ token }) , credentials: 'same-origin' }) and render 'Signed in as <email>' on 200 or the error on failure, again via textContent. Include a 'Sign out' button that posts to /auth/logout and reports the result. Never write the token into the DOM or into console output.

README.md: replace the line stating there is no login with a 'Authentication' section describing the passwordless magic-link flow (request -> email with token, 15-minute single-use token -> verify -> 24h HttpOnly session cookie -> logout), list the endpoints POST /auth/request, POST /auth/verify, POST /auth/logout, GET /me, GET /login with their status codes, and note that in this demo emails are captured in memory (MemoryEmailSender) rather than delivered. Keep the existing Install/Run/Test sections.

tests/login-page.test.ts (vitest) must: (1) request GET /login via createApp().request('/login') and assert status 200 and a Content-Type header containing 'text/html'; (2) assert the body contains '/auth/request', '/auth/verify', '/auth/logout', 'type="email"', and 'id="status"'; (3) assert the body does NOT contain '<script src', '<link ', 'innerHTML', or 'onsubmit='; (4) read README.md with node:fs/promises and assert it mentions '/auth/request' and no longer contains the phrase 'There is no login or auth of any kind'.
Only edit files in scope.allowed_paths. No new npm dependencies, no changes to package.json or src/.
non_goals: Do not implement or modify any server route, session or token logic.
No SPA, bundler, CSS framework, or client-side routing.
No password fields, sign-up form or OAuth buttons.

POST /auth/request validates { email } with zod, rate-limits on trim+lowercase email before any user lookup, returns 400 / 429 / 202 with the fixed bodies, and never reveals whether the email exists (identical 202 body, no token/userId in responses or logs).

POST /auth/verify validates { token }, exchanges it via magicLinks.verify, creates a 24h session, sets an HttpOnly SameSite=Lax Path=/ cookie (Secure only on https) and returns the user serialized like GET /users/:id; bogus/reused tokens get 401.

GET /me resolves the session cookie via sessions.get and users.findById, returning exactly 401 { error: 'not authenticated' } when absent/expired/revoked/user missing; POST /auth/logout revokes if present, always clears the cookie and returns 204.
GET /login reads public/login.html via new URL('../public/login.html', import.meta.url) and returns 200 text/html or 404 { error: 'login page not found' }; I will not create that file.

Write tests/auth-routes.test.ts covering the ten required cases hermetically with an injected now and MemoryEmailSender, using createApp().request(...) only, and keep tests/app.test.ts green (I do not expect to need to edit it).
assumptions: src/auth/magic-link.ts and src/auth/rate-limit.ts are present and match the described API (verified: they are, from t-magic-link-core commit a516b1f); I consume them unchanged.
The token in the email text can be extracted from the 'Or enter this token: <token>' line (or the ?token= query in the link) written by MagicLinkService.
public/login.html does not exist in this worktree, so test (10) will assert the 404 branch, in a way that also accepts 200 text/html if the file is later present.
The normalized email (trim + lowercase) is passed to magicLinks.request; UserRepo normalizes emails itself so behaviour is identical.
Cookie parsing/serialization is done with getCookie/setCookie/deleteCookie from 'hono/cookie'; the Secure flag is derived from new URL(context.req.url).protocol.
risks: Hono's setCookie may serialize SameSite as 'Lax' and Max-Age formatting slightly differently than expected; tests assert the substrings the contract names ('session=', 'HttpOnly', 'SameSite=Lax', 'Path=/').
zod 4 email validation could reject unusual but valid addresses; the seeded test addresses are simple so this does not affect the tests.
The rate limiter counts every attempt including the 429ed ones; this matches the spec (6th request within the window is 429).
